audience.description: Solo creators and small business owners who post short videos every week. They have a camera roll full of clips they never finish editing, they are short on time, and they care about looking polished and consistent without hiring anyone or spending evenings in a timeline.

brief.productRole: The app is the hero of the story. A creator picks a handful of raw clips from a messy camera roll, chooses a 15 second length, and taps once. The phone screen shows the clip blocks snapping into a tidy timeline with cuts and captions landing on the beat. The creator then nudges one clip, trims a caption, and taps post. The app edits their own footage only.
brief.mood: Relieved, quick, quietly confident, with a small payoff of satisfaction

music.style: Upbeat indie electronic pop with a clean four on the floor kick, plucky synth arpeggios, finger snaps and a light bass. Modern and bright, with a small drum fill on the final cut.

visual.look: Natural bright daylight grade with soft warm highlights and gentle sage and cream tones. Handheld phone-native vertical framing at eye level, shallow depth of field on close-ups of the phone screen, light grain. Fast pacing: a cut every 1 to 1.5 seconds, with the cuts matching the music beat. Opens on a chaotic scrolling camera roll, then the visual rhythm tightens as the edit snaps together. Screen close-ups use abstract colored blocks only, no readable text.

wardrobe.styling: Everyday creator casual: oversized plain knit sweater in oatmeal, a plain washed denim jacket, a simple apron in canvas for the shop owner, plain t-shirts in muted earth tones. No logos, no printed text, minimal jewelry.

types: sunlit small home studio corner with a desk and ring light
small independent ceramics shop with shelves of handmade mugs
cozy apartment couch with a laptop closed beside it

voice.tone: Friendly, direct and a little wry, like a smart friend who respects your time
use: Speaks to the viewer's weekly posting routine
Names the simple steps: pick clips, pick a length, tap
Points out that the edit is fully adjustable before posting
Ends with a plain invitation to try it and mentions $9.99 a month
avoid: Claiming it generates people or writes ads
Hype words like game-changing or revolutionary
Invented ratings, user counts or testimonials
Speaking as a customer who tried it

hooks: Your camera roll is not a video yet.
Forty clips. One tap. Fifteen seconds.
Stop editing at midnight. Post by lunch.

talent.description: Two fictional adults. One is an adult solo creator in their mid twenties with a relaxed, quick-witted energy, filming at a desk. The other is an adult small business owner in their early thirties, practical and warm, in a ceramics shop. Both react with small genuine smiles of relief as the edit appears.
